summary.text: Case 1 is a pregnancy with maternal age 27, maternal BMI 42, gravidity 3 and parity 1. The Maternal Rhesus type cell is printed + and the Maternal Antibody cell −. The pregnancy involved a single fetus (number of fetuses 1). As one of the 10 cases meeting the inclusion criteria, she had placentomegaly on ultrasound and maternal edema on clinical examination; all women showed hemodilution and rapid weight gain.

Fetal hydrops was diagnosed at gestational age 31 + 1 and Mirror Syndrome at gestational age 31 + 1. Hematocrit at delivery was 20%. The table lists a diagnosis to birth interval of 5 days without stating which diagnosis starts that interval.

Birth occurred at gestational age 31 + 6. The Birthweight below 10th centile cell is printed –. Days until maternal improvement is listed as 2, and maternal clinical features improved within 5 days postpartum in all instances in this series.

As one of the 10 cases meeting the inclusion criteria, she had placentomegaly on ultrasound and maternal edema on clinical examination; all women showed hemodilution and rapid weight gain.

Birth occurred at gestational age 28 + 2. The Birthweight below 10th centile cell is printed –. Days until maternal improvement is listed as 2, and maternal clinical features improved within 5 days postpartum in all instances in this series.

summary.text: Case 7 is a pregnancy with maternal age 30, maternal BMI 20, gravidity 1 and parity 0. The Maternal Rhesus type cell is printed – and the Maternal Antibody cell + Anti-D. The pregnancy involved a single fetus (number of fetuses 1). As one of the 10 cases meeting the inclusion criteria, she had placentomegaly on ultrasound and maternal edema on clinical examination; all women showed hemodilution and rapid weight gain.

Fetal hydrops was diagnosed at gestational age 29 + 5 and Mirror Syndrome at gestational age 29 + 5. Hematocrit at delivery was 19%. The table lists a diagnosis to birth interval of 15 days without stating which diagnosis starts that interval.

Birth occurred at gestational age 31 + 6. The Birthweight below 10th centile cell is printed –. Days until maternal improvement is listed as 3, and maternal clinical features improved within 5 days postpartum in all instances in this series.

article_limitations: Only Table 2 gives per-case data. Table 2 is a JATS text table (its rendered image duplicates the same cells and is described only in visual.json); per-case facts cite the text cells. Tables 3, 4 and 5 and most of the Results text are cohort statistics and are not copied to individual cases, except explicit all-case statements (all 10 cases met the inclusion criteria; all women had hemodilution and rapid weight gain; maternal features improved within 5 days postpartum in all instances).

Table 2 has no legend defining the + and - symbols. Maternal Rhesus type and Maternal Antibody cells keep the printed symbol as text with a positive/negative flag for these qualitative blood-bank results; Birthweight <10th centile cells keep the printed symbol as text with no flag; the twin-case cells -/NA and -/+ are unresolved text with an ambiguity.

The Diagnosis to birth (days) header does not say whether the interval starts at fetal hydrops or Mirror Syndrome diagnosis; no start point is inferred from arithmetic on the printed gestational ages.

Cohort medians in the text differ from Table 2 medians (hydrops diagnosis 19 weeks 2 days in the text versus 22 + 3 in Table 2; Mirror Syndrome diagnosis 22 weeks 3 days in the text and discussion, 23 weeks 3 days in the abstract, 24 + 1 in Table 2; diagnosis to birth median 8 days range 1-48 versus median 7 in Table 2; Table 3 hemoglobin and albumin ranges differ from Table 5). These are aggregate inconsistencies, not individual facts, and are not reconciled.

Several etiologies and outcomes (sacrococcygeal teratoma, CPAM, hypoplastic left heart syndrome, cystic hygroma, TTTS, incomplete molar pregnancy with dilation and evacuation, coxsackie virus B3, mode of delivery and labour induction per case, stillbirth and neonatal death per infant, hypertension, preeclampsia, hypoalbuminemia, anemia, hyperuricemia, proteinuria, thrombocytopenia, dyspnea) are stated only as cohort counts and are not attributed to labeled cases; only the Rhesus isoimmunization pregnancy (Case 7) and the TRAP pregnancy (Case 4) are kept as review-only facts with ambiguities.
Ten patients are the mothers of the ten pregnancies; fetuses and newborns stay in the mother record with subject fetus or newborn.
